title: Rust fragmentation timeout hold-down starts from stale DIO receipt time
description: FragmentSender timeout_current/timeout_with_authority release an aborted session using peer.receipt_ticks(), which is the DIO policy receipt timestamp, not the current timeout/terminal time. For a long-running sender the 60k-tick tombstone can already be expired when installed, allowing delayed prior-session controls into immediate tuple reuse. Require current authenticated/local monotonic time at terminal timeout and test long session, exact boundary, regression, std/no_std parity.
notes: Hold-down/reservation comparisons also use the old peer DIO receipt time at construction and receiver allocation; both start/end timing must use a current monotonic sample in a defined unit.
